groups.title: PJM show cause proceeding (E-7)
groups.about: The E-7 order asks whether PJM’s tariff stays just and reasonable without large-load rules on the five reforms. Everything filed in EL26-67 since June 18: the 30-day report, abeyance requests and the order granting them, answers and comments.

link.text: This is the E-7 docket itself. PJM and its transmission owners must defend the tariff or file changes; after abeyance, responses are due Nov 16, 2026.

groups.status: SPP answered on Nov 18 and 19 with three section 205 filings in new dockets, ER27-559, ER27-577 and ER27-578. Its letters say a response in this docket covers transmission and ancillary service rates for co-located load; it was not on this sheet through Nov 20.

link.text: This is the E-9 docket itself. SPP and its transmission owners must defend the tariff or file changes; after abeyance, responses are due Nov 20, 2026.

groups.status: Valley Electric asked on Nov 13 to be dropped from the order. CAISO says it will file by Nov 16.

link.text: This is the E-10 docket itself. CAISO and its transmission owners must defend the tariff or file changes; after abeyance, responses are due Nov 16, 2026.

groups.status: ISO-NE answered on Nov 13 with a section 205 filing in a separate docket, ER27-484. Nothing new is on this sheet through Nov 15.

link.text: This is the E-11 docket itself. ISO-NE and its transmission owners must defend the tariff or file changes; after abeyance, responses are due Nov 16, 2026.

groups.title: Filed in several show cause dockets
groups.about: Interventions, comments and motions that one party filed in more than one of the six show cause dockets.

link.text: Each of these was filed in two or more of the six show cause dockets, so it answers several orders at once.

groups.title: PJM co-location compliance
groups.about: Co-location means a large load, usually a data center, built at a power plant and served partly by it. FERC set rules for it in PJM; these filings carry them out.
groups.status: PJM filed partial compliance Aug 17, 2026 and answered three limited protests Oct 14. On Nov 16 PJM moved to withdraw that filing and refiled revised changes in ER27-531; the PJM Transmission Owners say their Nov 16 filing in ER27-520 also meets their compliance obligation here.

link.text: E-2, decided the same day as the six orders, finalized PJM’s three co-location transmission services; the six orders point to them as the model. PJM’s compliance filing is due Nov 16, alongside E-7.

groups.title: PJM Large Load definition, Registry and Interim Resource Adequacy Service
groups.about: PJM asked FERC to define a Large Load, keep a registry of them, and create a service that would curtail such loads first in a supply emergency. FERC kept the definition and the registry and rejected the rest.
groups.status: PJM filed compliance on Nov 9. Ohio’s consumer advocate and the PJM Industrial Customer Coalition each asked FERC that day to revisit the order. Comments on compliance are due Nov 30 at 5 p.m. Eastern.

link.text: Defines which PJM loads count as large and how PJM learns about them, which every application and study rule in E-7 depends on. Filed under section 205, outside EL26-67.

groups.title: PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement
groups.about: PJM, the grid operator for 13 states and D.C., proposed a backstop purchase of new power plants to cover a projected supply shortfall as large loads grow. On Sep 29 FERC accepted it for filing, suspended it to Feb 28, 2027 subject to refund, and set three cost issues for a paper hearing.
groups.status: FERC suspended the procurement on Sep 29. PJM filed amendments Oct 29, refiled them Nov 9 under the §205 code in ER27-454-000, and moved on Nov 12 to withdraw the Oct 29 filing. Comments are due Nov 30 at 5 p.m. Eastern.

link.text: PJM’s July 20 E-7 adequacy report presents this procurement, begun before the order, as its main resource-adequacy effort.

groups.title: Rehearing of FERC's PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement order
groups.about: Seven parties ask FERC to reconsider its September order accepting PJM's backstop procurement. Asking for rehearing is the required step before a party can take an order to court.
groups.status: Seven requests, filed Oct 13 to Oct 29, 2026. FERC had not ruled on any as of Nov 9.

link.text: Challenges to FERC’s September order on the backstop procurement, which PJM’s E-7 adequacy report presents as its main resource-adequacy effort.

groups.title: Exelon complaint seeking a prompt PJM capacity auction
groups.about: Exelon, whose utilities serve more than 10.7 million customers in PJM, asks FERC to run PJM's capacity auction two months before each delivery year instead of three years ahead.
groups.status: Filed Nov 3, 2026. On Nov 13 FERC gave PJM until Dec 21 to answer; comments and interventions are due the same day. Exelon asks for an order by Jan 31, 2027.

link.text: A separate section 206 complaint on capacity-auction timing; it bears on the resource-adequacy topic of E-7’s 30-day report.

groups.title: MISO Large Load Addition Resource Study (LARS)
groups.about: MISO, the grid operator for 15 states in the Midwest and South, wants to study a new load of 200 MW or more together with the power plant built to serve it. The proposed study runs about 120 days and sits outside its multi-year generator queue.
groups.status: MISO answered protests on Nov 9 and asked FERC to accept LARS. Six consumer advocates asked on Nov 12 for conditions on acceptance. The requested effective date is Dec 2.

link.text: MISO is answering E-8 in separate section 205 filings. LARS studies a large load and the generation built to serve it together, MISO’s answer to the order’s proximate-generation item.

groups.title: MISO zero-injection generator interconnection agreement
groups.about: MISO proposed a generator interconnection agreement for generation that serves on-site load and injects nothing into the grid. FERC staff found the filing deficient on Oct 9 and asked for more information.
groups.status: FERC staff issued a deficiency letter on Oct 9, 2026.

link.text: A MISO section 205 filing for generation that serves on-site load and injects nothing into the grid. It creates no new transmission service; MISO lists it among its pieces answering E-8.

groups.title: MISO interconnection reliability requirements for large loads
groups.about: MISO proposed reliability requirements that large loads must meet to connect. State regulators, consumer advocates and clean-energy groups protested; data centers, industrial customers and municipal utilities answered.
groups.status: Answers through Nov 3, 2026; no FERC order as of Nov 12.

link.text: MISO says this filing is responsive to concerns raised in EL26-70: the ongoing operating requirements a large load must meet once connected, E-8’s first item.

groups.title: ATC large-load planning revisions (Attachment FF-ATCLLC)
groups.about: American Transmission Company, which plans its own local system inside MISO, filed large-load interconnection criteria for loads of 100 MW or more in its Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota and Michigan footprint. Microsoft protested that large retail customers are left out of the process; MISO filed comments and a limited protest. ATC agreed in its answer to apply some criteria from 50 MW.
groups.status: FERC staff sent a deficiency letter on Oct 15, 2026 asking about load aggregation, storage charging load and which reliability rules govern when ATC's and MISO's differ. No response on the docket sheet as of Nov 18.

link.text: ATC filed under paragraph 36 of the E-8 order, which lets MISO transmission owners make their own section 205 filings.

groups.title: SPP conditional large-load service credits (CHILLS)
groups.about: SPP proposed revenue credits for conditional large-load service in its western zones, then corrected one rate sheet on Nov 10. A separate Aug 24 filing (ER26-3591) changes the CHILL policy for planned outages; FERC found it deficient Oct 21 and SPP answered Nov 19.
groups.status: ER27-432 filed Nov 6 and amended Nov 10, 2026. ER26-3591 deficiency response filed Nov 19.

link.text: SPP extends CHILLS, the conditional large-load service E-9 builds on, to its West Region. The filing does not cite E-9 or EL26-68.

groups.title: Duke Energy Carolinas network service agreement and large-load shortfall payments
groups.about: Duke Energy Carolinas' network service agreement adds a payment from customers of 100 MW or more who use less transmission than they committed to.
groups.status: Accepted Oct 9, 2026, effective Aug 1, 2026.

link.text: A non-RTO utility writing minimum-charge protections for large loads into a network service agreement, the same cost-shift protection the orders ask RTOs to consider.

groups.title: 2026 FERC reliability technical conference: integrating large loads
groups.about: FERC's annual reliability conference, run by the commissioners. Its first panel covered running the grid with fast-growing large loads such as data centers.
groups.status: Held Oct 21, 2026, with Panel 1 on integrating large loads.

link.text: FERC’s technical conference on integrating large loads reliably, including the flexible operation the orders’ new services depend on.

groups.title: PJM governance and stakeholder reform vote
groups.about: After FERC's July conference on how PJM makes decisions, PJM's members voted on a reform package. PJM told FERC the states do not find the result satisfactory.
groups.status: PJM reported the Members' Sept 30, 2026 vote to FERC on Oct 1. The Board has not said what it will file.

link.text: PJM governance reform runs beside the orders: who decides PJM’s section 205 filings, including its E-7 response.

groups.title: PJM stakeholder record on its show cause response
groups.about: Documents from PJM’s own stakeholder process as it prepared its show cause response: Members Committee agendas, the legal report and a letter from large customers to the PJM Board.
groups.status: PJM consulted members on Nov 5, 2026. Its matrix for that meeting says it will file under section 205 on or about Nov 16.

link.text: The stakeholder process PJM ran before deciding what to file in response to E-7 by Nov 16.

groups.title: ISO-NE large-load tariff revisions
groups.about: ISO New England, the NEPOOL Participants Committee and the region’s transmission owners filed tariff rules for loads of 50 MW or more at one site: firm, interim and non-firm service, a study process, and a cost recovery agreement that NEPOOL did not support. They ask FERC to end the E-11 show cause case.
groups.status: Filed Nov 13, 2026. Comments are due Dec 4 at 5 p.m. Eastern; ISO-NE asked for Dec 7 and FERC has not ruled on that.

link.text: The section 205 filing ISO-NE and its transmission owners promised on Oct 9 in answer to E-11. It was made in a new docket, ER27-484, and asks FERC to terminate the show cause proceeding.

groups.title: PJM Transmission Owners’ large-load tariff revisions
groups.about: The PJM Transmission Owners filed rates, a pro forma cost recovery agreement and a cost allocation method for upgrades serving large and co-located loads. PJM’s own companion filings are separate.
groups.status: Filed Nov 16, 2026. A Nov 18 errata notice moved comments from Dec 7 to Jan 15, 2027 at 5 p.m. Eastern, matching PJM’s ER27-531.

link.text: The section 205 filing the PJM Transmission Owners promised on Oct 9. It answers the E-7 show cause order and, the owners say, meets their E-2 co-location compliance obligation in EL25-49.

groups.title: PJM large-load tariff revisions
groups.about: PJM filed a 12-month Fast Energization Process that studies generators and large loads together, three new transmission services, a 50 MW cap on netting behind-the-meter generation, and, in a second filing, ride-through and operating requirements for large computational loads.
groups.status: Filed Nov 16, 2026. FERC’s Nov 18 notice sets comments due Jan 15, 2027 on ER27-531 and Dec 7 on ER27-522, at 5 p.m. Eastern.

link.text: PJM’s section 205 answer to the E-7 show cause order. ER27-531 also refiles PJM’s E-2 co-location compliance changes, replacing the Aug 17 filing it withdrew the same day.

groups.title: MISO large-load tariff revisions
groups.about: MISO and its transmission owners filed a Large Load Project Review study process, two cost recovery agreements, a large-load dashboard and two new services. A separate MISO filing creates GRITS, a permanent firm and non-firm contract demand service that cannot start before 2029.
groups.status: Filed Nov 16, 2026. FERC’s Nov 18 notice sets comments due Dec 16 on ER27-526 and Dec 7 on ER27-527, at 5 p.m. Eastern. Community and clean energy groups asked Nov 18 for 30 more days on ER27-526.

link.text: MISO’s section 205 answer to the E-8 show cause order, filed with its earlier LARS, zero-injection and reliability-requirements filings.

groups.title: CAISO and California transmission owners’ large-load tariff revisions
groups.about: CAISO filed a 50 MW large-load definition, co-location disclosure and a Flexible Interim Load Interconnection service, then refiled the same documents under a different filing code (ER27-532). Fifteen California transmission owners filed their own tariff revisions in separate dockets, where deposits, security and cost recovery sit.
groups.status: Filed Nov 16, 2026. Comments are due Dec 7 on ER27-506 and on most transmission owners’ filings, Dec 9 on ER27-506-001 and Dec 16 on ER27-532, at 5 p.m. Eastern. Constellation asked Nov 19 for nine more days on the PG&E, SCE and SDG&E filings.

link.text: The section 205 answers of CAISO and its participating transmission owners to the E-10 show cause order.

groups.title: NYISO and New York transmission owners’ large-load tariff revisions
groups.about: NYISO filed Large Load Integration Procedures, Firm and Non-Firm Withdrawal Service in place of the three PJM-style services, and market rules for large loads. The New York transmission owners (ER27-529) and LS Power Grid New York (ER27-518) filed cost recovery terms separately.
groups.status: Filed Nov 16, 2026. A Nov 18 errata notice moved comments on ER27-517 from Dec 7 to Dec 14 at 5 p.m. Eastern. The New York transmission owners’ ER27-529 comments are due Dec 7.

link.text: NYISO’s section 205 answer to the E-12 show cause order, with the transmission owners’ companion filings.

groups.title: SPP large-load tariff revisions
groups.about: SPP filed three sets of tariff changes it says answer E-9: transmission service and operating rules for High Impact Large Loads (ER27-559), a Load Safe Harbor Limit on network upgrade costs (ER27-577), and Price Adaptive Load Service, a non-firm service for loads that bid as dispatchable demand (ER27-578).
groups.status: Filed Nov 18 and 19, 2026. Comments are due Dec 9 on ER27-559 and Dec 10 on ER27-577 and ER27-578, at 5 p.m. Eastern.

link.text: SPP’s section 205 answer to the E-9 show cause order, filed in three new dockets two days before its Nov 20 deadline.

groups.title: Senate oversight hearing on FERC, July 22, 2026
groups.about: Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee oversight hearing with the FERC commissioners, including questions on the large-load orders.

link.text: Commissioners explained the June orders to Congress, under questioning about cost, timing and state authority.
